summary: Implement human rights due diligence, UNGPs compliance, and ESG reporting. Build practical frameworks to navigate global issues and supply chain risks.
lede: Human rights instruments training helps compliance, ESG and supply chain professionals apply international standards to operational risks. They learn to structure due diligence, assess supplier labor and digital or environmental impacts, design grievance and remediation processes, and record findings in risk registers and ESG disclosures.
audienceIntro: This program is engineered for professionals responsible for translating international human rights standards into corporate operational reality. It serves practitioners who must navigate complex regulatory environments, manage supply chain risks, and ensure ethical compliance across global operations.
modules: Supply Chain Transparency and Labor Rights
Environmental Human Rights and Climate Justice
prerequisites: Participants should have a foundational understanding of corporate compliance, ESG principles, or international law. Prior experience in risk management, sustainability reporting, or supply chain auditing is highly recommended. No formal legal qualification is required, but familiarity with corporate governance structures will be beneficial.
